newsitem.title: USA: Nash Finch to acquire Super Food.
newsitem.headline: Nash Finch to acquire Super Food.

text.p: Nash Finch Co., the fourth largest public grocery wholesaler, has reached a definitive agreement to acquire Super Food Services Inc. in a cash tender offer worth $173.6 million, the companies said Tuesday.
The merger will create the nation's third-largest public grocery wholesaler, with estimated sales of about $4.5 billion in 1997, they said.
Under the agreement, which has been approved by both companies' boards, Minneapolis-based Nash Finch will offer $15.50 for each of Super Food's 11.2 million shares outstanding.
Super Food's stock rose $4 to $15.25 on the New York Stock Exchange. Nash Finch edged up 25 cents to $15.75 on Nasdaq.
"We expect the acquisition to be accretive to earnings for calendar year 1997," said Al Flaten, Nash Finch's president, in a statement.

"There is no significant geographic overlap of operations. Super Food has significant market presence in Ohio, Michigan, Indiana and Kentucky, while Nash Finch has especially strong operations in the Midwest and Southeast market areas."
Dayton, Ohio-based Super Food supplies food and non-food products to more than 850 retail stores in six states.

Nash Finch supplies products to affiliated and independent supermarkets, other independent retailers and military bases in about 30 states. It also owns and operates about 110 supermarkets, warehouse stores and mass merchandise stores in 16 states, and a produce marketing subsidiary in California.
